text.p: The law minister in Pakistan's caretaker government resigned on Wednesday citing differences with President Farooq Leghari and caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid.
It was not immediately known if Leghari had accepted the resignation of Fakhruddin Ibrahim, the law, justice and parliamentary affairs minister, ministry officials said.

Ibrahim's resignation letter, copies of which were released to reporters, cited "unjustified interference" in his work, disagreement on changes made to new electoral laws and a senior appointment in the Law Ministry as reasons for his action.

"Because of certain pressures the government thought it necassary for political reasons to further amend the amendments introduced in the election law. I was unhappy with the proposed amendments and had to put to you my submissions in a forceful manner," he said.
"It is a matter of regret that my point of view was not accepted and the government promulgated certain amendments which have made the earlier amendments controversial."
Ibrahim also said he could not understand why the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court insisted on the appointment of his nominee as the secretary to the Law Ministry.

Ibrahim was the second member of the caretaker cabinet to resign this week. Syeda Abida Hussain, the education, science and technology and tourism minister, quit on Monday to contest general elections set for February 3.

Ibrahim, a former Supreme Court judge, joined the caretaker cabinet after Leghari dismissed Benazir Bhutto's government on disputed charges of corruption and misrule and dissolved the National Assembly (lower house) on November 5.
